flagged.evidence: Step 1.3 asserts: 'the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in the y-variable gives ∫_Y|k(x,y)f(y)|dν(y) ≤ (∫_Y|k(x,y)|²dν)^{1/2}‖f‖₂ for every x, and integrating with respect to x and applying Cauchy–Schwarz in L²(μ) to the function x ↦ (∫|k(x,y)|²dν)^{1/2} gives ∫_{X×Y}|k(x,y)f(y)|d(μ×ν) ≤ ‖k‖₂‖f‖₂ < ∞ by [A4]'. That displayed inequality is false. Take X=[0,4] and Y=[0,1] with Lebesgue measure, k ≡ 1 ∈ L²(μ×ν) and f ≡ 1 ∈ L²(ν); then ‖k‖₂ = 2 and ‖f‖₂ = 1, but ∫_{X×Y}|k(x,y)f(y)|d(μ×ν) = 4 > 2 = ‖k‖₂‖f‖₂. Cauchy–Schwarz in L²(μ) applied to h(x) = (∫_Y|k(x,y)|²dν)^{1/2} against the constant function 1 yields only μ(X)^{1/2}‖k‖₂‖f‖₂, so the written bound needs μ(X) ≤ 1, and it fails for every σ-finite space with μ(X) > 1. Step 2.1 then appeals to 'the bound of step 1.3' to put (x,y) ↦ k(x,y)f(y)·conj(g(x)) into L¹(μ×ν) so that Fubini applies; that bound would not give this even if it were true, because g ∈ L²(μ) need not be bounded. The correct estimate ∫∫|k f g|d(μ×ν) ≤ ‖k‖₂‖f‖₂‖g‖₂ (Cauchy–Schwarz in the y-variable, then in L²(μ) against |g|) is available but nowhere displayed, so the boundedness of K and the adjoint computation are not justified as written although both are true.

Claim 3 asserts: 'if J ⊆ I contains it and σ : ℕ → J is a surjection, then the sequence of partial sums Σ_{k<n}⟨x,e_{σ(k)}⟩e_{σ(k)} also converges to x'. A surjection may repeat values, and then the listed terms are not partial sums along distinct basis vectors. Counterexample: H = ℂ, I = {0}, e₀ = 1 is a complete orthonormal family, x = 1; the support is {0}, take J = {0} and the surjection σ(k) = 0 for all k. Then Σ_{k<n}⟨x,e_{σ(k)}⟩e_{σ(k)} = n·1, which diverges instead of converging to x = 1. Step 2.1 depends on the false reading in the clause 'the second because its coefficients are a subfamily of the tail and Pythagoras applies': a repeated index i contributes multiplicity |σ⁻¹(i) ∩ [0,n)| to the coefficient of e_i, and that multiplicity is unbounded, so the terms are not a subfamily of the tail. The claim is true only for injective σ (a bijection of ℕ onto J); neither the Statement nor the proof imposes or establishes injectivity, and the closing sentence 'any enumerating sequence of a set containing the support is cofinal in the squared mass' does not repair it.

coverage_note: Opened and read from disk all 67 carriers of the computed refuter_scope exactly once: the 63 items plus the four page files (library/functional-analysis/hilbert-space-geometry-and-riesz-representation.md, its -examples companion, orthonormal-bases-parseval-and-fourier-series.md, and its -examples companion). For every item I checked the title, Statement/Definition, each Facts row against the cited clause where load-bearing, and every numbered step against the fact, earlier step, hypothesis or elementary computation offered in its support, including the direction and quantifiers of the variational inequality, the first-variable-linear convention, the complex case, and the empty-family, zero-vector, one-dimensional, finite-torus and endpoint cases. Computations were re-derived independently: both polarisation identities, the parallelogram and minimising-sequence estimates, the Gram system G^T c = b with its basis independence, the mean and distance formulas, the first three Legendre members with the 8/45 normalisation, the Haar orthonormality and dyadic level spans, character orthonormality on T^n, and both Fourier examples (coefficients, ‖f‖₂², Basel π²/6 and Leibniz π²/8); all agree with the items. The reader's three repairs (E1 in lem-trigonometric-characters-are-orthonormal step 2.1, E2 in thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus step 1.1, E3 in ex-fourier-series-of-a-square-wave) are present and correct in the current files, and their conclusions are unchanged. Dependencies were opened where a scoped claim needed the clause (the L¹ Fubini statement, lem-countable-iff-surjection-from-n, def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set, thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family, thm-jordan-von-neumann-polarization for the uniqueness of the inducing inner product, and the choice-convention items); two defects were found and are flagged. Limitations: I read cited published suppliers at the level of the cited clause rather than re-proving them from their own hypotheses, and I did not re-verify book page/lecture/URL locators against the sources themselves. Small gaps examined and judged nonfatal rather than flagged, none of them a defective claim, definition, title or citation: thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace step 2.1 obtains Im⟨x-p,u⟩=0 from w=p+itu only after the same u↦−u substitution already used one clause earlier for the real part; lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive step 3.1 and thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family [A4] say 'linearity in the second argument' where only additivity of the conjugate-linear slot is used; ex-standard-basis-of-ell-two step 1.2 uses completeness of the scalar field without naming the published theorem; and the examples-page phrase 'for every exponent other than the Hilbertian one' was read as ranging over the rational exponents the example actually states. No other defect found in the scope.
